question: naming.class.jim-source-member-chronology-control
problem: What public Jim class-package results follow sequential external method declarations, two-word procedures before/after a class factory, and BASES references to current, moved, command-aliased, deleted or nonclass command names?

questions.question: Do both sequential external method definitions remain callable on a newly constructed object?
Are genuine two-word procedures written before and after the class factory both publicly reachable on a new object?
Does moving an earlier two-word procedure away withdraw that original class-member route?
Does a current BASES name import the original method and class-variable defaults?
Does moving only the class dispatcher preserve inherited two-word targets at the moved name?
Does an ordinary command alias used as a BASES name supply inherited two-word routes?
Can a known deleted base dispatcher supply a new class factory?
Does replacement by a nonclass procedure permit base-list factory execution, and what public result follows?

channel: Original fixed ASCII LF CLI file; package require oo availability, caught public class/object results. Source contains no raw or counted NUL, non-ASCII, line continuations or control escapes. No internal object/header/native argv/cache/frame/currentness claim. C stock class-command absence is not applicable, separate from TclOO availability.
authority_boundary: Observed public class-package behaviour is independent of conditional Compiler class-reference and metadata carriers; even a successful alias BASES outcome would not license Native class-object identity in those carriers.
